correctness.rationale: For each prescribed three-color word the indicator expansion is exact outside 0,-1,-2; exclusion term lies in [0,27]. Nontrivial single-root terms vanish, the 12 two-root sums have Weil bound sqrt(p), and the 8 three-root sums have bound 2sqrt(p). Consequently 27N >= p-28sqrt(p)-27 > 0 at p>=841. The exact finite verifier exhausts every one of the 70 eligible primes p<=840 by two independent coset labelings, proves all eligible p>=307 pass, and finds the sole missing 000 word at 283. The symbolic infinite-tail argument and actual code paths were reconstructed and checked.

originality.rationale: The 1962 theorem proves only that the final prime missing three consecutive cubic residues is 283; a complete simultaneous 27-word conclusion is strictly stronger, demonstrably independent at p=151 and 163 where 000 occurs but 202 is absent. The full 1970 Rabung-Jordan paper treats any single monochromatic coset. Hu-Chen and Yuan-Zhang count a±a^{-1} configurations. Targeted indexed-literature searches disclosed no full 27-word threshold; older Lehmer (1983) was inaccessible in full and remains a concrete priority risk.

Unindexed or non-English older results and future human proof review could alter originality attribution; this review is not a claim of publication priority.

value.rationale: Simultaneous realization of every length-three word in the canonical three-color cubic-residue language is a motivated full-alphabet strengthening of the 1962 triple-of-cubes problem. It has a sharp universal admissible-prime threshold: 307 is the first admissible prime after the final 283 obstruction, and all other 26 words must be shown too; at 151 and 163 the prior all-zero criterion already holds while full completeness fails. The result completely resolves this natural finite-word invariant for all eligible primes, but does not imply longer-word coverage or frequency formulas.
